The writer effectively uses sensory details—particularly regarding sight, temperature, and sound—to create a tangible and believable setting. For example, the text appeals to the sense of touch and temperature by contrasting "cold and wet weeks" ("naßkalten Wochen") with a "false midsummer" ("falscher Hochsommer") that makes the park feel "stifling/muggy as in August" ("dumpfig wie im August"). Visually, the writer paints a vivid picture of the "delicately leafed" trees, the "sinking sun," the "gleaming" ("gleißend") tram tracks on the paved street, the monuments in the stonemason's yard, and the "reflection of the departing day" ("Abglanz des scheidenden Tages") on the Byzantine building. Auditory details are also present, moving from the lively beer garden down "quieter and quieter paths" ("stillere und stillere Wege") to the mortuary hall lying "silently" ("schweigend").
